title: "Moment constraints and principal representations"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Moment constraints and principal representations}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(principalMoments)
```

The first `v` moments generally leave many compatible distributions. The two
principal representations are special finite distributions matching those
moments. Their nodes and weights depend on the moments, not on the integrand.

```{r}
m <- 1 / (2:4) # Uniform(0,1) moments
reps <- principal_representations(m)
reps$lower
reps$upper
reps$diagnostics
```

For odd `v = 2n-1`, these are Gauss and Lobatto rules. For even `v = 2n`,
they are left and right Radau rules. For feasible boundary moments, both
representations coincide with the unique compatible distribution.

```{r}
principal_representations(c(0.3, 0.09))$lower # point mass at 0.3
principal_representations(c(0.3, 0.3))$upper # Bernoulli distribution
```

For a continuous integrand whose derivative of order `v+1` is nonnegative,
the lower rule minimises its expectation and the upper maximises it among
all compatible distributions. Negative derivative sign reverses the roles.
The caller must establish this condition: it is not numerically tested.

```{r}
functional_bounds(reps, exp, derivative = "positive")
# The actual expectation under Uniform(0,1) lies between these values:
exp(1) - 1
```

In clustered group testing, write `Q = 1 - (1-P)^s` for the probability of a
positive pool at a location. Observing the count law for `v` pools identifies
the first `v` moments of `Q`. Marginal individual prevalence is
`E[1 - (1-Q)^(1/s)]`. For `s > 1`, the required derivatives are positive on
`(0,1)` and the integrand is continuous on `[0,1]`. Endpoint derivatives need
not be finite for this application of the Chebyshev-system condition.

```{r}
f <- function(q, s) -expm1(log1p(-q) / s)
functional_bounds(reps, f, s = 25, derivative = "positive")
```

For other functions, evaluate without claiming extrema:

```{r}
evaluate_representations(reps, function(x) sin(10 * x))
evaluate_representations(reps, function(nodes, weights) {
  sum(weights * nodes^2) - sum(weights * nodes)^2
}, type = "distribution")
```

General support intervals require raw moments on that same interval:

```{r}
# Uniform(-1, 1): mean 0 and second moment 1/3
principal_representations(c(0, 1/3), support = c(-1, 1))$lower
```

Raw-moment inversion is ill-conditioned for high orders or near boundary
sequences. Inspect residuals and eigenvalue diagnostics, and assess sensitivity
to `tol`. Residuals describe agreement with the input, not forward accuracy
of individual nodes. The package rejects infeasible inputs and unresolved
numerical inversion problems rather than discarding higher moments.

The algorithms follow Karlin and Studden (1966), *Tchebycheff Systems*;
Krein and Nudelman (1977), *The Markov Moment Problem and Extremal Problems*;
and Gautschi (2004), *Orthogonal Polynomials*, Section 1.4.2.
